# Corporate Travel & Expense Policy

## 1. Purpose
This document defines reimbursement rules for all employee travel and
incidental business expenses. It supersedes all prior travel policy
memos and applies to every domestic and international trip booked
after the effective date below.

## 2. Effective Date
This policy takes effect for all trips booked on or after January 1.
Trips booked before that date follow the legacy 2025 policy, archived
separately and not covered here.

## 3. Booking Procedure
All flights and hotels must be booked through the corporate travel
portal. Exceptions require director-level sign-off submitted in
writing before the trip, not after. Employees who book outside the
portal without prior approval may have reimbursement denied entirely,
regardless of the amount.

## 4. Daily Category Caps
Reimbursable expenses are capped per category, per day, as follows:

- Lodging: $200 per night, before taxes and mandatory resort fees.
- Meals: $45 per day, inclusive of tips.
- Ground Transport: $60 per day, covering taxis, rideshare, and
  parking combined.
- Incidentals (laundry, wifi, etc.): $25 per day.

Any single day's spend in a category above its cap must be justified
in writing by the traveler's manager or it will not be reimbursed.
Caps are per category, not pooled across categories — an employee
cannot spend less on meals to justify more on lodging.

## 5. Per Diem Alternative
Employees on trips longer than 5 consecutive nights may elect a flat
per diem of $300/day covering meals, transport, and incidentals
combined (lodging is always itemized separately regardless of trip
length). Once elected, per diem cannot be mixed with itemized receipts
for the same trip.

## 6. Receipts
Any single expense over $25 requires an itemized receipt, not just a
credit card statement line. Missing receipts over this threshold
result in automatic denial of that line item during audit.

## 7. International Travel
International trips add a $50/day incidentals allowance on top of the
domestic incidentals cap, due to currency conversion friction and SIM
card costs. All other caps remain unchanged for international travel.

## 8. Audit & Enforcement
Finance audits 100% of trips over $1,500 total and a random 10% sample
of smaller trips monthly. Any category found over cap without written
manager justification is clawed back from the employee's next payroll
cycle, not merely flagged.

## 9. Questions
Route policy interpretation questions to the Finance shared inbox, not
to individual approvers, so answers stay consistent across the
company.
